newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Leningrad orders study into new cargo airport.
newsitem.headline: Leningrad orders study into new cargo airport.

text.p: The local authority of Russia's Leningrad region said on Friday it had commissioned a feasibility study from a U.S. firm on turning a former military air base into an international cargo airport.
Airis Development Group Inc should finish by October the study of Veshchevo air base, 150 km (100 miles) northwest of the regional capital, St Petersburg.

The regional authority said in a statement that the new airport could have capacity of 400,000 to 450,000 tonnes of cargo per year after possible modernisation to make it the first cargo-only airport in Europe.
Officials said earlier this year the upgrade would cost $250 million. After the feasibility study, the U.S. firm will seek investors for the project.
